summary:
[  edit  ]
The  CHOP  to  TOP  puts  CHOP  channels into a  TOP  image. By default the texture created will be 32-bit floating point to match the precision of the  CHOP  data. This can be changed setting the  TOP 's Pixel Format to something other than 'Input'.
The Data Format parameter determines how the input channels are converted into pixel colors in the output image. For example, when the Data Format is set to 'R', each channel will be interpreted as a row of red pixel data. Likewise, if the Data Format is RGBA, then the first 4 channels will become a set of red, blue, green and alpha data for one row of pixels and each subsequent set of 4 channels will become additional rows.  Note:  Channels are grouped by their order in the  CHOP  rather than their names i.e. just because a channel is named g0 or b1 does not mean it will necessarily be be placed in a blue or green pixel.
The Image  Layout  parameter controls how the pixel rows are arranged in the output image. By default, the width of the image will be equal to the number of samples in the  CHOP , clamped to a maximum texture width (often 32768) (the sample rate is ignored), and the height will be equal to the number of channel sets. For example, when the Data Format is RGB and the there are 9 input channels (for example, r0 g0 b0 r1 g1 b1 r2 g2 b2), there will be 3 rows of pixels using the default image layout.
If the channel length is longer than the image width, the wrapped layout option can be used to continue the channel data onto additional rows of pixels. Each new set of channels will still begin on a new row of pixels.
If the Image  Layout  parameter is set to Fit to Square, the  TOP  determines the image resolution based on the total number of samples across all channel sets (approximately the square root of the number of samples + 1) in width and height. This layout is most often used for point cloud data, where an efficient layout is preferred and the position of a pixel is not generally important. Unlike in the wrapped layout, channel sets in this mode are appended immediately to the end of the previous set, so that any empty pixels will appear at the end of the image.  Where there are some unused pixels, you can fill the unused pixels at the top with a special value based on the Extra Pixel Values parameter, (0, 0, 0, 0) by default. To put (0, 0, 0, -1) you have to set the pixel format to 32-bit float so you can represent negative and positive numbers of any value.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: The path of the  CHOP  being referenced.

parameters.label: Data Format
parameters.name: dataformat
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the input  CHOP  channels will be turned into an image. If the  CHOP  is missing channels required to provide all the data for a scanline, the extra channels are ignored.

parameters.label: R
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Each channel is treated as the Red channel for a new scanline. Using the default Image  Layout , the height of the image will be equal to the number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: RG
parameters.name: rg
parameters.description: The first two channels will be the Red and Green channels for a scanline, the next two channels will be Red and Green for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image  Layout , the height of the image will be half the number of channels in the  CHOP , rounded down.

parameters.label: RGB
parameters.name: rgb
parameters.description: The first three channels will be the Red, Green and Blue channels for a scanline, the next three channels will be Red, Green and Blue for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image  Layout , the height of the image will be the number of channels in the  CHOP  divided by 3, rounded down.

parameters.label: RGBA
parameters.name: rgba
parameters.description: The first four channels will be the Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha channels for a scanline, the next four channels will be Red, Green, Blue and Alpha for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image  Layout , the height of the image will be the number of channels in the  CHOP  divided by 4, rounded down.

parameters.label: A
parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Each channel is treated as the Alpha channel for a new scanline. Using the default Image  Layout , the height of the image will be equal to the number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Legacy
parameters.name: legacy
parameters.description: This mode only creates a single scanline in all cases. More than 4 channels will not do anything. If the  CHOP  has 1 or 2 channels, it will set R,G,B,A to the first channel of the  CHOP . The 2nd channel is ignored. If it has 3 channels, it sets the 3 channels to R,G,B and A = sample number / # of samples (i.e A is a ramp starting at 0 and climbing to the (width -1). If it has 4 channels, they are set to R,G,B,A.

parameters.label: Clamp  CHOP  Values
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: Clamps  CHOP  values to 0-1 range.

parameters.label: Image  Layout
parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls the dimensions of the output image and how the  CHOP  samples are arranged as pixels. This menu replaces the previous 'Crop Long Channels' and 'Fit to Square' parameters.

parameters.label: Row per Channel Set (Cropped)
parameters.name: rowscropped
parameters.description: Each set of channels, as determined by the Data Format, is converted into a row of pixels in the output image. If the channel length exceeds the maximum texture resolution, or the custom width defined in the Output  Resolution , the remaining samples are  ignored . This option is equivalent to turning on the previous Crop Long Channels parameter.

parameters.label: Row(s) per Channel Set (Wrapped)
parameters.name: rowswrapped
parameters.description: Each set of channels, as determined by the Data Format, is converted into a row of pixels in the output image. If the channel length exceeds the maximum texture resolution, or the custom width defined in the Output  Resolution , the remaining samples will be put  into a new row of pixels . Additional channel sets will begin in a new row of the output rather than at the end of the previous set. This option is equivalent to turning off the previous Crop Long Channels parameter.

parameters.label: Fit to Square (Combine Sets)
parameters.name: square
parameters.description: Pixels are arranged in the smallest square texture that fits all of the given  CHOP  samples. Channel sets, as determined by the Data Format, are wrapped onto the next row of pixels if the  CHOP  channel length exceeds the width of the texture. Unlike the wrapped layout, the next channel set will begin at the next available pixel rather than starting in a new row. This option is equivalent to turning off the old 'Crop Long Channels' parameter and turning on the previous 'Fit to Square' parameter. This layout is most often used for point cloud data, where the position of a pixel in the image is not generally important.

parameters.label: Extra Pixel Values (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba
parameters.description: ⊞  - If the current Image  Layout  results in more pixels than there are available samples in the input  CHOP , the values specified here will be used to fill in the extra pixels. (All textures require full rows of pixels, in other words all rows of pixels have the same number of pixels.)

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).
